# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0001 (first iteration of the run)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: shipped 4 edits in one candidate after FIRST
  reverse-engineering the reward model from the tau2 evaluator source rather than guessing
  from trajectories. The single highest-leverage META move was reading evaluator.py /
  evaluator_communicate.py / tasks.py to establish that reward = DB × COMMUNICATE with
  ACTION UNSCORED. That reframed the whole search: the target is not "make the agent call
  the right tool with the right args" but "make the resulting DB correct (in-body compute)
  and make the required number appear in a message (relay-ready return)". No LEDGER rows
  yet (result stamped after stop).
- Plateau/stall signal: none (first iteration). Reward starts 0.222 (2/10 solid).
- What worked in the PROCESS: (a) confirm the scoring model from source before designing —
  cheap, and it invalidated the naive "fix the agent's arguments" framing; (b) offline
  execution of each new tool body against the pristine DB in the tau2 venv gave a
  deterministic VERIFIED signal without a full rollout; (c) fan-out diagnosis subagents
  (grouped by cluster) + one dedicated passing-task-baseline subagent made the SAFE check
  concrete (I had 8/37's exact trace args to re-run).
- What to try next iteration (if there is one):
  1. Read the RESULT stamp: if the new tools did NOT get called by the runtime agent (check
     whether reward moved on 11/12/17/22/40), the lever to switch is tool NAME/description
     SALIENCE, not more code — a perfect body the agent never selects is dead weight.
  2. For the mid-cap reader (aws/gpt-oss-120b), consider whether `preview_flight_change_cost`
     and `list_user_reservations` need their descriptions to explicitly say "call this FIRST
     when the user describes a route / asks the cost" — selection, not capability, is the
     likely residual failure.
  3. 23/25 remain structurally unfixable without overfitting; do not spend an iteration
     re-attempting them with a task-specific literal — the held-out gate rejects that.
